results.title: Perception data system for satellite monitoring of strategic assets
results.abstract: Considering the different ways of applying nanosatellites, their inherent cost advantages, and the fact that this field represents a strategic area, the development of the Perception system for data collection via satellite is proposed. The Perception is a system for monitoring and producing strategic assets that uses the CubeSat standard as an instrument for the transition from scientific research to the product of technological innovation for sustainable development. Specifically, we aim to create a concept of operation, bringing the digital twin approach to deliver, among others, a new small satellite simulation environment based on the hardware-in-the-loop concept integrating the STK software, Helmholtz cage, air bearing top tables, and a flat satellite with an SDR payload for store-and-forward applications. The expected outcomes include a structured engineering model to define and validate the architecture of complex systems based on the CubeSat standard. The pilot project is aimed at collecting data via satellite from the K34 Tower of the Large-Scale Biosphere-Atmosphere Program in the Amazon (LBA), whose data is used to monitor carbon flow, among other applications. The K34 Tower is in the Amazon rainforest, approximately 64km from Manaus city, Brazil. Applications aimed at tracking unmanned aerial vehicles that support environmental monitoring activities will also be considered. Moreover, the restructuring of the entire Laboratory of Simulation and Control of Aerospace Systems, LODESTAR, at the University of Brasília is being guided by the concepts and methods of the Perception system, seeking to innovatively integrate the digital twin concept into its new physical and logical architecture. This work presents an overview of the Perception data system, its main architectures and systems, and future contributions.
